reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) supports that O and N promote phase segregation, α-Ti precipitate formation, and matrix softening during 700°C aging, but it does not provide evidence for brittle intergranular precipitates, crack initiation, or loss of toughness under mechanical loading; these key premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Interstitial O and N promote phase segregation during aging at 700°C in TiVNbTa
Segregation leads to precipitate formation, specifically α-Ti precipitates
Precipitate formation depletes the matrix of strengthening solutes, causing softening
Brittle precipitates form along grain boundaries and act as crack initiation sites
Impurity-doped samples will show reduced toughness and brittle fracture compared to high-purity baseline
